61
RAJYA SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL  ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday, the July 20, 2004/Asadha 29, 1926 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Civil Aviation; Company Affairs; Finance; Panchayati Raj;
Petroleum and Natural Gas; Tourism; Water Resources)
Total number of questions—20
ONGC's joint venture in Sudan
*201. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that commercial
production of crude oil in Sudan through
joint  ventures  of  ONGC  Videsh  and
Sudanese Government has started;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the quantity and the rate at which
crude oil from Sudan will be made available
to India?
Transactions by big firms in NSE and
BSE
†*202. SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD: Will the Minister of FINANCE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that out of the
total transactions carried out in NSE and
BSE during the first six months of the year
2003-04, over 50 per cent contribution was
made by ten big firms only;
(b) if so, the facts in this regard; and
(c) the names of such ten big firms
which made the maximum contribution in

the transactions of the said exchanges
togetherwith the percentage of their
contribution in terms of the total
transactions?
Modernisation of Madurai Airport
*203. SHRI C. PERUMAL: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
modernise and expand Madurai airport and
also to start aircraft operations from Salem
airport in Tamil Nadu; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?
Budgetary flexibility in States
*204. SHRIMATI JAMANA DEVI
BARUPAL:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Reserve Bank of India
has called upon States to make efforts to
enhance their own revenues-both tax and
non-tax, to improve budgetary flexibility;
(b) if so, whether any concrete steps in
this regard have been considered by
Government; and

(c) what are the suggestions made by
RBI to the States and how many States
have agreed to augment their revenues?
Fiscal deficit of NE States
*205. SHRI RISHANG KEISHING:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased
to state:
(a) the financial deficit of each of the
seven States in N.E. Region during Financial
Year 1999-2000;
(b) the details of the States' financial
position as on today; and
(c) in what manner, the Central
Government propose to assist the States
to overcome their financial problem?
Increase in account maintenance
charges
*206. SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA: Will the Minister of
FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether National Security
Depository Limited sponsored Depository
Participants have increased Account
Maintenance charges from Rs. 75/- p.a. to
Rs. 150/- p.a. and then to Rs. 300/-p.a.
during the last three years;
(b) whether this increase has been
approved by proper communication to
customers (shareholders/investors); and
(c) if not, what action Government
propose to take to stop this arbitrary
increase so that such an action can help in
reviving the stock markets?
LNG terminal at Mangalore
*207. SHRI K.B. KRISHNA
MURTHY: Will the Minister of
PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether ONGC proposes to sign a
Memorandum of Understanding with
Karnataka Government to set-up an LNG
Terminal at Mangalore coast;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) by when, it will be set-up?
Debt relief to farmers
*208. PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Ministry of Finance
after declaring measures/package for
agriculture, has directed the States to work
out targets for boosting loan credit and
provide debt relief to distressed farmers;
(b) if so, whether Chief Ministers of
States have been urged to implement action
plan announced by the Central
Government;
(c) if so, whether Government are
confident that measures announced will
only be implemented with the cooperation
of State Governments; and
(d) if so, what is the progress so far
made by States and how many States have
agreed to meet the target fixed in this regard?
Increase in area under irrigation
*209. SHRIMATI SARLA
MAHESHWARI: Will the Minister of
WATER RESOURCES be pleased to state:
(a) what is the increase in the land area
under irrigation during the last three years;
(b) whether Government are having any
short-term plan for the extension of
irrigation facilities; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?

Feeder airline in West Bengal
696. SHRI SHANKAR ROY
CHOWDHURY: Will the Minister of
CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Central Government has
received any proposal from the
Government of West Bengal for establishing
a feeder airline within the State; and
(b) if so, the action proposed to be taken
in this regard alongwith the present position
of the case?
Advance Passenger Information
System
697. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Ministry
of Civil Aviation has sent a note to the
Cabinet for its approval for introduction
of Advance Passenger Information System
which helps the immigration officials to
get information about the passengers well
before the aircraft reaches its destination;
(b) whether it is also a fact that the
Ministry of Civil Aviation proposes to do
away with baggage X-Ray of incoming
passengers; and
(c) if so, the reasons therefor?
Server3/1205RS raw text/1205rs.6.5 159
Revamping of Alliance Air's fleet
698. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the Indian Airlines has taken
a decision to go in for dry leasing of A-319
aircrafts to revamp the fleet of its wholly-
owned subsidiary-Alliance Air;
(b) if so, the details in this regard and
the salient features of A-319 aircrafts; and
(c) the terms and conditions of the
agreement to be signed in this regard?
Investigation in helicopter crashes
699. SHRI R.K. ANAND: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that serious lapses
of omission by Directorate General of Civil
Aviation (DGCA) were traced in the
investigation conducted in the helicopter
crashes in Jammu and Kashmir and off the
Mumbai coast last year; and
(b) if so, what action Government have
taken against DGCA to check recurrence
of such incidents in future?

CAT-3 Landing System at IGI Airport
700. SHRI ANAND SHARMA: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the CAT-3 Landing System
has been made fully operational at the Indira
Gandhi International Airport, New Delhi;
(b) if so, what are the reasons for the
delay in takeoffs and landings during winter
season; and
(c) the number of Air India flights
cancelled or diverted out of Delhi during
December-January, 2003 and the additional
costs incurred by Air India as a result
thereof?
Revival of Rupsee Aerodrome in
Assam
701. SHRI URKHAO GWRA
BRAHMA: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have any plan
to revive the Rupsee Aerodrome of Assam;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Overstaffing in Indian Airlines
702. SHRI SHAHID SIDDIQUI: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether there is a proposal to buy
new Aircrafts for Indian Airlines and Air
India;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is a fact that the number
of ground staff for aircrafts in Indian
Airlines is much higher than that of private
Airlines;
(d) if so, the reasons therefor: and
(e) whether Government have any
proposal to reduce the strength of staff in
the Government-managed airlines?
New International Airport in Navi
Mumbai
703. SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether a project proposal for
development of an International Airport at
Navi Mumbai through public-private
participation was submitted by the State
Government of Maharashtra;
(b) if so, when and what are the details
thereof; and
(c) the steps since taken thereon?
Restructuring of Delhi and Mumbai
airports
704. SHRI JANARDHANA
POOJARY: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to refer to answer
to Unstarred Question 29 given in the Rajya
Sabha on 6th July, 2004 and state the details
of the overseas and Indian companies that
have evinced interest in the restructuring
of Delhi and Mumbai airports?
Loss incurring airports
†705. SHRI MOTILAL VORA: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a number of
airports in the country are incurring losses;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and

to meet the losses?
